questions.text: Which one does not belong to the group: Punjab, Lahore, Karachi, Peshawar?
questions.explanation: Karachi, Lahore and Peshawar are cities, while Punjab is a province.

questions.text: Which one does not belong to the group: Iron, Copper, Bronze, Aluminium?
questions.explanation: Copper, iron and aluminium are pure metallic elements; bronze is an alloy of copper and tin.

questions.text: Which one does not belong to the group: Rose, Mango, Lily, Jasmine?
questions.explanation: Rose, lily and jasmine are flowers; mango is a fruit.

questions.text: Which one does not belong to the group: Eye, Ear, Nose, Lung?
questions.explanation: Eye, ear and nose are sense organs; the lung is a respiratory organ.

questions.text: Which one does not belong to the group: Sparrow, Emu, Ostrich, Kiwi?
questions.explanation: Ostrich, emu and kiwi are flightless birds; the sparrow can fly.

questions.text: Which one does not belong to the group: Square, Rectangle, Triangle, Rhombus?
questions.explanation: Square, rectangle and rhombus have four sides; the triangle has three.

questions.text: Which one does not belong to the group: Litre, Metre, Gallon, Pint?
questions.explanation: Litre, gallon and pint measure volume; the metre measures length.

questions.text: Which one does not belong to the group: Indus, Jhelum, Chenab, Karakoram?
questions.explanation: Indus, Jhelum and Chenab are rivers; Karakoram is a mountain range.

questions.text: Which one does not belong to the group: Cotton, Wheat, Rice, Maize?
questions.explanation: Wheat, rice and maize are food grains; cotton is a fibre crop.

questions.text: Which one does not belong to the group: April, June, August, September?
questions.explanation: April, June and September have 30 days each; August has 31.

questions.text: Which one does not belong to the group: Mercury, Moon, Venus, Mars?
questions.explanation: Mercury, Venus and Mars are planets; the Moon is a natural satellite.

questions.text: Which one does not belong to the group: Hammer, Screwdriver, Saw, Nail?
questions.explanation: Hammer, saw and screwdriver are tools; a nail is a fastener worked on by tools.

questions.text: Which one does not belong to the group: Sahara, Amazon, Nile, Danube?
questions.explanation: Nile, Amazon and Danube are rivers; the Sahara is a desert.

questions.text: Which number does not belong to the group: 3, 5, 9, 7?
questions.explanation: 3, 5 and 7 are prime numbers, while 9 is composite (3 x 3).

questions.text: Which number does not belong to the group: 8, 100, 27, 64?
questions.explanation: 8, 27 and 64 are perfect cubes of 2, 3 and 4; 100 is not a perfect cube.

questions.text: Which number does not belong to the group: 49, 64, 81, 80?
questions.explanation: 49, 64 and 81 are the squares of 7, 8 and 9; 80 is not a perfect square.

questions.text: Which number does not belong to the group: 21, 17, 13, 19?
questions.explanation: 13, 17 and 19 are prime; 21 is divisible by 3 and 7.

questions.text: Which number does not belong to the group: 15, 25, 42, 35?
questions.explanation: 15, 25 and 35 are multiples of 5; 42 is not.

questions.text: Which number does not belong to the group: 4, 20, 16, 8?
questions.explanation: 4, 8 and 16 are powers of 2; 20 is not.

questions.text: Which number does not belong to the group: 121, 144, 169, 180?
questions.explanation: 121, 144 and 169 are the squares of 11, 12 and 13; 180 is not a perfect square.

questions.text: Doctor is to Patient as Lawyer is to:
questions.explanation: A doctor renders professional service to a patient just as a lawyer does to a client.

questions.text: Pen is to Write as Knife is to:
questions.explanation: The pair links an instrument with its function: a pen is used to write, a knife to cut.

questions.text: Bird is to Nest as Bee is to:
questions.explanation: The relation is creature to its dwelling: a bird lives in a nest, a bee in a hive.

questions.text: Foot is to Shoe as Hand is to:
questions.explanation: A shoe is the covering worn on the foot, as a glove is the covering worn on the hand.

questions.text: Cat is to Kitten as Dog is to:
questions.explanation: The relation is adult to young: a young cat is a kitten and a young dog is a puppy.

questions.text: Teacher is to School as Judge is to:
questions.explanation: The relation is professional to workplace: a teacher works in a school, a judge in a court.

questions.text: Thermometer is to Temperature as Barometer is to:
questions.explanation: Each instrument is paired with what it measures; a barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

questions.text: Island is to Water as Oasis is to:
questions.explanation: An island is land surrounded by water, and an oasis is a fertile patch surrounded by desert.

questions.text: Sculptor is to Statue as Poet is to:
questions.explanation: The relation is maker to the work produced: a sculptor makes a statue, a poet composes a poem.

questions.text: Circle is to Sphere as Square is to:
questions.explanation: A sphere is the three-dimensional counterpart of a circle, and a cube is that of a square.

questions.text: Carpenter is to Wood as Blacksmith is to:
questions.explanation: The relation is craftsman to the material worked upon: a carpenter works with wood, a blacksmith with iron.

questions.text: Ship is to Captain as Aeroplane is to:
questions.explanation: The relation is vehicle to the person who commands it; an aeroplane is flown by a pilot.

questions.text: Frog is to Amphibian as Snake is to:
questions.explanation: The relation is animal to its class; the snake belongs to the class of reptiles.

questions.text: Deaf is to Hearing as Blind is to:
questions.explanation: A deaf person lacks hearing, and a blind person lacks sight.

questions.text: Pakistan is to Islamabad as Turkey is to:
questions.explanation: The relation is country to capital; Ankara, not Istanbul, is the capital of Turkey.

questions.text: Wheat is to Flour as Sugarcane is to:
questions.explanation: The relation is raw crop to the product processed from it; sugarcane yields sugar.

questions.text: Novel is to Chapter as Poem is to:
questions.explanation: A chapter is a division of a novel, as a stanza is a division of a poem.

questions.text: Zoology is to Animals as Botany is to:
questions.explanation: Each branch of science is paired with its subject matter; botany is the study of plants.

questions.text: Ornithology is to Birds as Entomology is to:
questions.explanation: Ornithology is the study of birds and entomology is the study of insects.

questions.text: Melting is to Liquid as Freezing is to:
questions.explanation: Melting produces a liquid, while freezing produces a solid.

questions.text: If 3 : 10 and 5 : 26, then 7 : ?
questions.explanation: Each second term is the square of the first plus 1, so 7 gives 49 + 1 = 50.

questions.text: If 2 : 5 and 4 : 9, then 6 : ?
questions.explanation: Each second term is twice the first plus 1, so 6 gives 12 + 1 = 13.

questions.text: If 3 : 12 and 5 : 30, then 7 : ?
questions.explanation: Each second term is the first multiplied by the next integer, so 7 gives 7 x 8 = 56.

questions.text: If 2 : 7 and 3 : 13, then 4 : ?
questions.explanation: The rule is n squared plus n plus 1, so 4 gives 16 + 4 + 1 = 21.

questions.text: If 5 : 24 and 7 : 48, then 9 : ?
questions.explanation: Each second term is the square of the first minus 1, so 9 gives 81 - 1 = 80.

questions.text: If 2 : 8 and 3 : 27, then 4 : ?
questions.explanation: Each second term is the cube of the first, so 4 gives 4 x 4 x 4 = 64.

questions.text: If 6 : 18 and 8 : 32, then 10 : ?
questions.explanation: Each second term is half the square of the first, so 10 gives 100 / 2 = 50.

questions.text: If 9 : 3 and 25 : 5, then 64 : ?
questions.explanation: Each second term is the square root of the first, and the square root of 64 is 8.

questions.text: If 12 : 4 and 21 : 7, then 27 : ?
questions.explanation: Each second term is one third of the first, so 27 gives 27 / 3 = 9.
Each second term is the square of the first, so 13 gives 13 x 13 = 169.

questions.text: If 4 : 13 and 6 : 19, then 9 : ?
questions.explanation: Each second term is three times the first plus 1, so 9 gives 27 + 1 = 28.

questions.text: If 1 : 4 and 2 : 9, then 4 : ?
questions.explanation: Each second term is the square of one more than the first, so 4 gives 5 x 5 = 25.

questions.text: Aeroplane, helicopter and glider form one class. Which of the following belongs to the same class?
questions.explanation: All the given items are means of air transport, and a hot-air balloon also travels through the air.

questions.text: Copper, zinc and nickel form one class. Which of the following belongs to the same class?
questions.explanation: The three named substances are pure metallic elements, and cobalt is also an element, whereas bronze, brass and steel are alloys.

questions.text: Triangle, quadrilateral and pentagon form one class. Which of the following belongs to the same class?
questions.explanation: All three are polygons bounded by straight sides, and a hexagon is a six-sided polygon.

questions.text: Sparrow, crow and pigeon form one class. Which of the following belongs to the same class?
questions.explanation: The three named creatures are birds, and the parrot is also a bird, while a bat and a squirrel are mammals and a butterfly is an insect.

questions.text: Rupee, dollar and dinar form one class. Which of the following belongs to the same class?
questions.explanation: All three are currencies, and the riyal is likewise a currency.

questions.text: Kidney, liver and heart form one class. Which of the following belongs to the same class?
questions.explanation: The three named items are internal organs of the body, and the lung is also an organ.

questions.text: Mango, banana and apple form one class. Which of the following belongs to the same class?
questions.explanation: The three named items are fruits, and guava is also a fruit while the others are vegetables.

questions.text: Hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen form one class. Which of the following belongs to the same class?
questions.explanation: The three named gases are chemical elements, and helium is also an element, whereas the other options are compounds.

questions.text: Square, rhombus and rectangle form one class. Which of the following belongs to the same class?
questions.explanation: All three are four-sided figures, and a trapezium is also a quadrilateral.

questions.text: Poetry, drama and novel form one class. Which of the following belongs to the same class?
questions.explanation: The three named items are forms of literature, and the essay is also a literary form.

questions.text: Which pair of unit and quantity is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: The watt is the SI unit of power; the newton measures force, the joule energy and the pascal pressure.

questions.text: Which pair of scientist and discovery is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928; the other three pairings are false.

questions.text: Which pair of country and currency is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: The currency of Japan is the yen; China uses the yuan, Bangladesh the taka and Iran the rial.

questions.text: Which pair of animal and dwelling is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: A horse is kept in a stable; a lion lives in a den, a bee in a hive and a sparrow in a nest.

questions.text: Which pair of instrument and use is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: A hygrometer measures humidity; a seismograph records earthquakes, a lactometer checks the purity of milk and a barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

questions.text: Which pair of collective noun and group is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Bees move in a swarm; cattle form a herd, birds a flock and fish a shoal.

questions.text: Which pair of province and its capital is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Quetta is the provincial capital of Balochistan; the capitals of Sindh, Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa are Karachi, Lahore and Peshawar.

questions.text: Which pair of book and author is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Bang-e-Dara is the Urdu poetry collection of Allama Iqbal; Gulistan is by Saadi, Shahnama by Firdausi and Masnavi by Rumi.

questions.text: Which pair shows the same relationship as Cow : Calf?
questions.explanation: The relationship is adult animal to its young; the young of a horse is a foal.

questions.text: Which pair shows the same relationship as Doctor : Stethoscope?
questions.explanation: The relationship is worker to the tool he uses; a farmer uses a plough, while the other options name places.

questions.text: Which pair shows the same relationship as Kilogram : Mass?
questions.explanation: The relationship is unit to the quantity it measures; the ampere measures electric current.

questions.text: Which pair shows the same relationship as Hot : Cold?
questions.explanation: Hot and cold are opposites, and only ancient and modern are opposites; the other pairs are synonyms.

questions.text: Which pair shows the same relationship as Chapter : Book?
questions.explanation: A chapter is a part of a book, and a room is a part of a house; the other pairs place the whole before the part.

questions.text: In the table below every row follows the same rule: Row 1 is 4, 5, 20; Row 2 is 6, 3, 18; Row 3 is 7, 8, ?. What number replaces the question mark?
questions.explanation: The third entry of each row is the product of the first two, so 7 x 8 = 56.

questions.text: In the table below every row follows the same rule: Row 1 is 9, 4, 5; Row 2 is 12, 7, 5; Row 3 is 15, 6, ?. What number replaces the question mark?
questions.explanation: The third entry is the first minus the second, so 15 - 6 = 9.

questions.text: In the table below every row follows the same rule: Row 1 is 3, 5, 34; Row 2 is 4, 6, 52; Row 3 is 5, 7, ?. What number replaces the question mark?
questions.explanation: The third entry is the sum of the squares of the first two, so 25 + 49 = 74.

questions.text: In the table below every row follows the same rule: Row 1 is 6, 4, 20; Row 2 is 8, 3, 22; Row 3 is 9, 5, ?. What number replaces the question mark?
questions.explanation: The third entry is twice the sum of the first two, so 2 x (9 + 5) = 28.

questions.text: In the table below every row follows the same rule: Row 1 is 5, 4, 15; Row 2 is 6, 3, 12; Row 3 is 7, 5, ?. What number replaces the question mark?
questions.explanation: The third entry is the product of the first two minus the first number, so 35 - 7 = 28.

questions.text: In the table below every row follows the same rule: Row 1 is 8, 4, 6; Row 2 is 10, 6, 8; Row 3 is 14, 8, ?. What number replaces the question mark?
questions.explanation: The third entry is the average of the first two, so (14 + 8) / 2 = 11.

questions.text: In a 3 by 3 grid every row adds up to the same total: Row 1 is 8, 1, 6; Row 2 is 3, 5, 7; Row 3 is 4, 9, ?. What number replaces the question mark?
questions.explanation: Each row totals 15, and 15 - 4 - 9 = 2.

questions.text: In the table below every column follows the same rule: Column 1 is 5, 4, 21; Column 2 is 7, 9, 40; Column 3 is 8, 14, ?. What number replaces the question mark?
questions.explanation: The third entry is the square of the first minus the second, so 64 - 14 = 50.

questions.text: In the table below every row follows the same rule: Row 1 is 2, 3, 11; Row 2 is 4, 5, 29; Row 3 is 3, 6, ?. What number replaces the question mark?
questions.explanation: The third entry is the product of the first two plus their sum, so 18 + 9 = 27.

questions.text: In the table below every row follows the same rule: Row 1 is 18, 3, 6; Row 2 is 28, 4, 7; Row 3 is 45, 5, ?. What number replaces the question mark?
questions.explanation: The third entry is the first divided by the second, so 45 / 5 = 9.

questions.text: In the table below every row follows the same rule: Row 1 is 7, 2, 45; Row 2 is 9, 4, 65; Row 3 is 10, 6, ?. What number replaces the question mark?
questions.explanation: The third entry is the square of the first minus the square of the second, so 100 - 36 = 64.

questions.text: In the table below every row follows the same rule: Row 1 is 2, 4, 8; Row 2 is 3, 9, 27; Row 3 is 4, 16, ?. What number replaces the question mark?
questions.explanation: Each row gives a number, its square and its cube, so the missing entry is 4 cubed, that is 64.

questions.text: In the table below the middle number of each row is the average of the outer two: Row 1 is 4, 7, 10; Row 2 is 6, 11, 16; Row 3 is 9, ?, 21. What number replaces the question mark?
questions.explanation: The average of 9 and 21 is (9 + 21) / 2 = 15.

questions.text: A table records a shop's sales as Monday 120 units, Tuesday 150 units, Wednesday 90 units and Thursday 160 units. What is the average number of units sold per day?
questions.explanation: The total is 520 units over four days, and 520 divided by 4 is 130.

questions.text: A student's marks, each out of 100, are Urdu 72, English 65, Mathematics 88 and Science 75. What is his average percentage?
questions.explanation: The marks total 300 out of 400, so the average is 300 divided by 4, that is 75 per cent.

questions.text: A college enrolment table shows Arts 250 students, Science 400 students and Commerce 150 students. What percentage of the total enrolment is in Science?
questions.explanation: The total enrolment is 800, and 400 out of 800 is 50 per cent.

questions.text: A monthly budget table shows rent Rs 12,000, food Rs 9,000, transport Rs 3,000 and other items Rs 6,000. What fraction of the total expenditure is spent on food?
questions.explanation: The total expenditure is Rs 30,000, and 9,000 out of 30,000 equals 3/10.

questions.text: A rainfall table shows January 25 mm, February 40 mm, March 15 mm and April 60 mm. What is the difference between the highest and the lowest monthly rainfall?
questions.explanation: The highest is 60 mm in April and the lowest 15 mm in March, and 60 - 15 = 45 mm.

questions.text: A table shows that a town's population was 50,000 in 2010 and 65,000 in 2020. What was the percentage increase over the decade?
questions.explanation: The rise is 15,000 on a base of 50,000, and 15,000 divided by 50,000 is 30 per cent.

questions.text: A table of test marks out of 50 shows Ali 35, Bilal 42, Sara 28 and Hina 45. How many of the four scored more than 60 per cent?
questions.explanation: Sixty per cent of 50 is 30 marks, and Ali, Bilal and Hina all scored above 30.

questions.text: A production table shows unit A made 240 items and unit B made 180 items. What is the ratio of unit A's output to unit B's output?
questions.explanation: The ratio 240 to 180 reduces to 4 : 3 after dividing both numbers by 60.

questions.text: A table of daily maximum temperatures gives 30, 34, 28, 36 and 32 degrees Celsius for five days. What is the average daily maximum temperature?
questions.explanation: The five readings total 160 degrees, and 160 divided by 5 is 32 degrees.

questions.text: A library table shows books issued as Monday 45, Tuesday 60, Wednesday 35, Thursday 50 and Friday 60. On how many days were more than 45 books issued?
questions.explanation: Tuesday, Thursday and Friday exceed 45 books, so the answer is three days.

questions.text: A profit table shows Rs 8 lakh in 2019, Rs 6 lakh in 2020, Rs 10 lakh in 2021 and Rs 12 lakh in 2022. In which year did profit fall compared with the previous year?
questions.explanation: Profit dropped from Rs 8 lakh in 2019 to Rs 6 lakh in 2020, the only year showing a decrease.

questions.text: A staff table shows production 120 employees, sales 90, administration 60 and others 30. Sales staff form what percentage of the total staff?
questions.explanation: The total staff is 300, and 90 out of 300 is 30 per cent.
